chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Sahl, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that some of Quraysh said:
to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله: “By what thing did you precede the Prophets, while you were sent as the last of them and their seal?”
He said: “Indeed, I was the first of those who believed in my Lord, and the first of those who answered when Allah took the covenant of the Prophets and made them testify against themselves:”
“Am I not your Lord?” They said: “Yes.”
“So I was the first Prophet to say: ‘Yes’; thus I preceded them in acknowledging Allah.”

key_terms.الْأَنْبِيَاءَ: the Prophets addressed in the comparison
key_terms.بَلَى: yes indeed, the confirming response to the divine question
key_terms.بِرَبِّكُمْ: with your Lordship; Allah’s address affirming His Lordship
key_terms.خَاتَمَهُمْ: their seal, meaning the final one among them
key_terms.رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah, the Prophet Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله

ai.seo_question: How did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله precede the other Prophets despite being sent last?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله as preceding the other Prophets in his response to the divine covenant and in affirming faith in Allah. It presents his precedence not in terms of chronological earthly mission, but in the primordial acknowledgment of divine Lordship. The report also thematically relates to the Qur'anic covenant scene in which Allah addresses souls with His Lordship.
